assessments.result: Private mutex ownership removes the exported static shared PageMap reference and independently formed exclusive mutation alias. PageSnapshot contains Copy owned scalar fields; directory/stats/pin queries return scalars. Boot-copy validation releases map ownership before fallible allocation and raw copy. Its unsafe inventory-provenance, immutable-source and disjoint-growth requirements remain necessary. Snapshots are observations, not lifetime pins or physical authority. No scoped allocating callback is exported.

Production growth follows heap -> map -> frame. Prepare reserves heap backing before map -> frame. Examined frame-held callers release guards before heap/map diagnostics or formatting. Timer/keyboard and examined exception handlers do not acquire map/frame. SpinMutex does not mask interrupts: no-IRQ/no-reentrant-allocation remains a necessary architectural constraint, not a general IRQ-safe mutex guarantee.

Production reservations precede ownership. Frame operations and raw table writes allocate nothing. On recheck rejection or builder failure, owner is declared after backing and drops first; Vec destruction occurs unlocked. On validation failure the frame guard ends, then explicit drop(owner) precedes pm destruction. Success moves pm into an empty owner; remaining backing is empty. No production callback executes under the owner. cfg(test) MIRROR intentionally allocates under guards; host mirror behavior is not production allocation evidence.

Early unlocked publication check has an exclusive recheck before frame init. Builder exhaustion returns directory/table frames and clears table slots. Validation failure releases only unpublished paging structures and does not publish. Publication is a move with no subsequent fallible step. Growth checks map availability before claiming; map rejection restores growth-only reservation and preserves conflicting PTEs. Failed prepare reinitializes the allocator as before: boot-only initialization is not a transaction preserving arbitrary earlier allocator inventory.

Masking the low base word prevents base bits 24..31 from OR-contaminating access byte 5. Remaining base bytes, masked 20-bit limit, flags and access occupy independent architectural positions. Independent little-endian byte decode covers nonzero/boundary bases, limits, presence, DPL, system/type and flags. Exact current null/code/data constants are asserted unchanged. Encoding an available-TSS type is not installing or operating a TSS.

paging.rs and frame.rs are unchanged against HEAD. Boot PDE/PTE and growth entries remain supervisor-only. Unsupported USER/nonpresent requests still reject before table allocation. Effective PDE/PTE permission intersection, null/growth holes and CR0.WP activation are unchanged. This diff does not elevate kernel PDEs or add user mappings. Non-PAE NX remains unsupported.

Retained before/after snapshots exercise the former lifetime defect and assert identity, mapping count increment and supervisor permissions. B26 scalar-API substitutions preserve refusal/exhaustion/rollback accounting; publication-isolated subprocess fixtures remain. Independent byte decode is appropriate for the GDT fix. Two new gates mandate exact identities, observed multiplicity and exact passing/nonignored totals. Missing/zero/substituted evidence fails before publication. Predecessor gates and full-pipeline OS lock remain. Static method count is 39 and successful mocked-run expectation is 56 gates; neither establishes execution PASS. Tests do not prove cross-thread publication, CPU faults or remaining ownership.

inherited_blockers.severity: blocks owned address spaces and full Phase11A
inherited_blockers.finding: Public numeric allocator allocate/free/init and raw PageMap builders/map/unmap remain trusted kernel APIs, not nonduplicable capabilities. No allocator identity or ownership token binds physical payload/table lifetimes. A caller can free a live numeric frame, reuse it or reset the allocator without consulting a map. Synchronizing the private global map fixes retained Rust references, not this inherited physical ownership problem.
inherited_blockers.required_before_user_mappings: Explicit frame/table/payload ownership or bounded private ledger; active CR3/stack pins; alias validation; resource-owned publication rollback and teardown.

inherited_blockers.severity: blocks supported error-code exceptions, TSS/CPL3 and recovery
inherited_blockers.finding: Uniform one-argument x86-interrupt handlers still cover CPU error-code exceptions. Returning #GP lacks the separate error-code argument and is not a correct returning exception path. #PF embeds the hardware error word in its sole frame parameter rather than establishing a reviewed explicit error-code entry ABI. Generic exception frame storage is unimplemented. These unchanged, mostly fatal paths and ring-0 guest diagnostics do not prove CPL3 recovery.
inherited_blockers.required_before_transition: Explicit error/no-error entry conventions, register and segment preservation, correct CPU frame and stack-switch shape, fatal-kernel versus recoverable-user policy and safe kernel continuation.

inherited_blockers.finding: Only null and DPL0 code/data descriptors are installed. No TSS object, LTR, user descriptors, guarded owned transition stack, user IRET entry, syscall entry or controlled kernel continuation is implemented in the inspected paths. Source-wide searches found no TSS/LTR/user-IRET implementation. No CPL3 transition or security suite was executed by this reviewer.
